sources.excerpt: Published on April 4, 2012 Crushsound distortion/fuzz/overdrive modulation pedal Information The Crushsound Farmer's Mill is a handmade analog guitar effects pedal developed to produce controlled "broken sound" textures by introducing irregular signal degradation, interruption, and instability. Released in 2012 as an original design, it was conceived as a device that replicates the sonic characteristics of malfunctioning or damaged equipment, such as a failing cable or unstable amplifier behavior, while allowing the user to regulate the outcome. It functions as a stompbox with a footswitch that activates the effect during engagement, at which point the input signal is subjected to crushing, stuttering, and fragmentation processes referred to as "The Mill." The pedal combines multiple forms of signal alteration, including distortion-like saturation, bit reduction characteristics, and non-periodic modulation, resulting in a wide range of textures from subtle lo-fi artifacts to heavily disrupted output. Its circuit is designed to preserve the underlying tone of the instrument, allowing the processed signal to be layered with the dry signal rather than replacing it. The rate of signal disruption is adjustable but does not follow conventional tempo-based divisions, producing irregular and non-synchronized fluctuations. Operation centers on three controls and a four-stage mode selector integrated into the Mill control. The Mix control adjusts the proportion of processed signal, ranging from light surface noise resembling worn media to fully degraded output. The Rate control governs the speed of signal breaking, from slower interruptions to faster, more aggressive fragmentation. The Mill control selects between four distinct types of signal processing behavior, progressing from more stable and predictable responses to increasingly chaotic and less repeatable outcomes, with the final position producing an undefined state of maximum instability. The effect is active only while the footswitch is pressed, enabling momentary application of the processing. The concept originated with Jedrzej Lewandowski, who applied the idea of controlled demolition from architectural practice to sound processing. The electronic circuit was developed by Slawomir Badowski, while Lukasz Badowski contributed to the formation of Crushsound and the realization of the product. The pedal is constructed as a heavy-duty unit with a steel enclosure, powder-coated finish, and true bypass switching. Visual design and physical construction were developed with attention to balancing appearance and functional layout, including custom oxidized screws and a distinctive industrial finish. Controls Footswitch: Engages the effect while pressed; the signal is actively processed only during engagement Mix: Adjusts the level of processed signal blended with the dry signal Rate: Controls the speed and density of signal interruption and degradation Mill: Selects one of four modes of signal behavior, from controlled to increasingly chaotic Connections Input: 6.35 mm (1/4 inch) instrument input jack Output: 6.35 mm (1/4 inch) output jack DC Input: 9 V power supply input Technical Specifications Power Supply: 9 V DC, 100 mA Battery Operation: 9 V internal battery (active only when input jack is connected) Bypass Type: True bypass Enclosure Material: 1 mm steel Dimensions: 180 mm (7.1 inch) length, 150 mm (5.9 inch) width, 30 to 50 mm (1.2 to 2 inch) height Finish: Powder-coated cream white with black serigraphy; top screws oxidized in industrial oil Highlights Analog guitar effects pedal focused on controlled signal degradation and "broken sound" behavior Momentary footswitch operation for dynamic, performance-based activation Mix control enables blending of dry tone with degraded signal while maintaining tonal transparency Rate control provides non-synchronized, irregular signal interruption Four-position Mill control ranging from stable to fully chaotic processing True bypass switching and heavy-duty steel enclosure construction Video all | by manufacturer | not by manufacturer Date ▼▲ Maker ▼▲ Video ▼▲ Time ▼▲ 2013-10-02 Crushsound Crushsound - Farmer's Mill & Ceramic Slides - Commercial 2014 1:18 2013-10-02 Crushsound Crushsound - Farmer's Mill & Ceramic Slides - Commercial 2014 1:18 2013-08-24 Crushsound Crushsound | Farmer's Mill | Teaser | Low Range 0:27 2013-06-29 Crushsound Farmer's Mill 2013 teaser clip!
